title: Does Homogeneity Make Watermark/Provenance Attribution Harder?

original_idea.body:
# Does Homogeneity Make Watermark/Provenance Attribution Harder?

**Problem:** Distinguishing which model produced text underpins provenance and accountability. If outputs are homogeneous, attribution may be near-impossible.

**Direction:** Take outputs from several models on shared prompts and train a simple classifier to predict the source model. Relate attribution accuracy to measured inter-model homogeneity per prompt category.

**Why it matters:** If monoculture erodes the ability to tell models apart, post-hoc accountability for systemic events fails.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind; accountability framing in International AI Safety Report 2026.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible governance/accountability angle (attribution failure) but indirect link to catastrophic AI risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple classifier on embeddings to predict source model; very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: attribution accuracy vs homogeneity per category; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public outputs, cheap classifier; governance-relevant angle labs underweight.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference plus a small classifier; cheap.

novelty.reasoning: Authorship/source attribution studied; homogeneity-vs-attributability link partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Model attribution studied; relating it to homogeneity is a fresh framing.
